results.question: Let's establish the baseline: pull Newcastle United's (GB1) average league position per season from 2015 through 2024, using club_games own_position. I want to see the exact size and timing of the jump around the October 2021 takeover.

plan.intent: Newcastle United average league position per season 2015-2024
plan.sql: SELECT g.season, ROUND(AVG(cg.own_position),2) AS avg_own_position, COUNT(cg.own_position) AS games_with_position FROM club_games cg JOIN games g ON cg.game_id = g.game_id JOIN clubs c ON cg.club_id = c.club_id WHERE c.name LIKE 'Newcastle United%' AND g.competition_id = 'GB1' AND g.season BETWEEN 2015 AND 2024 GROUP BY g.season ORDER BY g.season

results.conclusion: Using club_games own_position for Newcastle United (GB1), the data shows a club stuck in lower-mid-table or worse from 2015 through 2021 (averaging between 12.63 and 17.92, with the 2016 relegation season missing entirely). The decisive shift lands between the 2021 season (16.55) and the 2022 season (4.50) — a ~12-position leap that coincides with the October 2021 takeover — and the elevated performance holds in 2023 (8.05) and 2024 (6.45). The magnitude and timing of the jump are clear from the numbers, giving a solid baseline for the takeover effect.

results.question: That back-half climb interests me. Newcastle both changed manager (Steve Bruce out, Eddie Howe in early November 2021) AND spent big in the January 2022 window. Using own_manager_name in club_games, split season 2021 by manager and show me average own_position under each — I want to see if the turnaround aligns with the managerial change.

plan.intent: Average own_position by manager within season 2021
plan.sql: SELECT cg.own_manager_name, COUNT(*) AS games, MIN(g.date) AS first_game, MAX(g.date) AS last_game, ROUND(AVG(cg.own_position),2) AS avg_own_position FROM club_games cg JOIN games g ON cg.game_id = g.game_id JOIN clubs c ON cg.club_id = c.club_id WHERE c.name = 'Newcastle United' AND g.season = 2021 GROUP BY cg.own_manager_name ORDER BY MIN(g.date)

The decisive move to top-of-table performance came in the subsequent full season under Howe and the new ownership, reinforcing that both the manager change and the January 2022 spending set up a delayed, compounding climb rather than an immediate one.

results.targets: Turn 4 manager channel vs Turn 6 squad-value channel timing
results.question: Now compare my two competing-explanation branches head to head. The manager branch (Turn 4) showed Howe only nudged 2021 position by ~2 spots, and the squad-value branch (Turn 6) showed the decisive 2022 jump landed on only a SMALL value increase, with the big money arriving in 2023-24 AFTER the climb. So which channel actually leads the initial 2021→2022 step-change — Howe's arrival or the investment — and which one merely sustains it later?

plan.intent: Line up Newcastle's YoY position change against YoY squad-value change to see which step-change carries the money and which carries the on-pitch leap.
plan.sql: WITH ncfc AS (SELECT club_id FROM clubs WHERE name LIKE 'Newcastle United%'), pos AS (SELECT g.season, ROUND(AVG(cg.own_position),2) AS avg_pos FROM club_games cg JOIN games g ON cg.game_id=g.game_id WHERE cg.club_id IN (SELECT club_id FROM ncfc) AND g.season BETWEEN 2021 AND 2024 GROUP BY g.season), val AS (SELECT season, ROUND(SUM(mv)/1e6,2) AS squad_val_m FROM (SELECT s.season, pv.player_id, pv.market_value_in_eur AS mv, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.season, pv.player_id ORDER BY pv.date DESC) AS rn FROM (SELECT unnest([2021,2022,2023,2024]) AS season) s JOIN player_valuations pv ON pv.current_club_id IN (SELECT club_id FROM ncfc) AND pv.date < make_date(s.season,8,1)) t WHERE rn=1 GROUP BY season) SELECT p.season, p.avg_pos, ROUND(p.avg_pos - LAG(p.avg_pos) OVER (ORDER BY p.season),2) AS pos_delta, v.squad_val_m, ROUND(v.squad_val_m - LAG(v.squad_val_m) OVER (ORDER BY p.season),2) AS val_delta FROM pos p JOIN val v ON p.season=v.season ORDER BY p.season

executed_sql: WITH ncfc AS (SELECT club_id FROM clubs WHERE name LIKE 'Newcastle United%'), pos AS (SELECT g.season, ROUND(AVG(cg.own_position), 2) AS avg_pos FROM club_games AS cg JOIN games AS g ON cg.game_id = g.game_id WHERE cg.club_id IN (SELECT club_id FROM ncfc) AND g.season BETWEEN 2021 AND 2024 GROUP BY g.season), val AS (SELECT season, ROUND(SUM(mv) / 1e6, 2) AS squad_val_m FROM (SELECT s.season, pv.player_id, pv.market_value_in_eur AS mv, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.season, pv.player_id ORDER BY pv.date DESC) AS rn FROM (SELECT UNNEST([2021, 2022, 2023, 2024]) AS season) AS s JOIN player_valuations AS pv ON pv.current_club_id IN (SELECT club_id FROM ncfc) AND pv.date < MAKE_DATE(s.season, 8, 1)) AS t WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY season) SELECT p.season, p.avg_pos, ROUND(p.avg_pos - LAG(p.avg_pos) OVER (ORDER BY p.season), 2) AS pos_delta, v.squad_val_m, ROUND(v.squad_val_m - LAG(v.squad_val_m) OVER (ORDER BY p.season), 2) AS val_delta FROM pos AS p JOIN val AS v ON p.season = v.season ORDER BY p.season LIMIT 1000
results.conclusion: Read head to head, the manager channel — Howe's arrival — leads the initial 2021→2022 step-change and the investment channel sustains it afterward. The decisive ~12-position leap (16.55 → 4.50) rode on only a moderate €123m squad-value bump, while the single biggest value increase (€151.5m into 2023) actually coincided with a slight position regression (+3.55) and the following year's smaller €48.9m rise merely held position flat. In other words, the money does not track the leap: the largest spending arrives after the climb and functions to sustain the elevated level, whereas the abruptly-timed on-pitch improvement lines up with the coaching change rather than with peak investment.
